snippet.textDisplay:
Same here—I’m caring for my dad in the advanced stages of Alzheimer’s. Sadly, it became too overwhelming to manage at home. I tried in-home care, but he made it very challenging for them to do their jobs. He would yell and threaten to hit them—not because they were mistreating him (I had cameras everywhere), but because, unfortunately, 30–50% of Alzheimer’s patients experience behavioral issues such as unpredictable aggression or inappropriate behaviors. On top of that, my dad struggled with severe insomnia.

As his care needs grew, caring for him became a 24/7 responsibility. That was my breaking point and the reason I transitioned him to memory care—though that, too, has its challenges. Even now, caring for my dad remains a big part of my life.

Everyone’s journey with Alzheimer’s is different, and we shouldn’t judge the decisions families make. What matters most is being supportive and kind.

Tip: If you ever reach the difficult decision to move a loved one into memory care, I highly recommend choosing a facility dedicated solely to memory care, as they are often better equipped to handle the complexities of dementia.

snippet.textDisplay: There’s a lot of reasons someone with dementia has to go to a care home. My grandpa recently moved to one because he kept leaving the house when my grandma wasn’t home. He would just walk and be gone for a few hours, no one knew where he was and it was terrifying. He also kept messing with his medical equipment and needed more intensive care. It’s not our fault that our parents/grandparents are unable to be cared for by us. If anything we are helping both them and us by doing this. It’s really hard but most of the time it’s the only option. I’m sorry you and everyone else is going through this. It’s never easy.

Memory care is the safest place for your beautiful mom. I’ve tried to keep my father at home but as his condition progressed, it became extremely difficult to get the care he deserved and needed.

He escaped from the home and went missing for a few hours. He was staying with my mom even though they were separated. She called frantically that he was gone. So my husband and I drove around looking for him and finally found him sitting on a tree bark. He loved trees. It was then that I realized I’m going to need some help with him.

You’re doing a wonderful job with your mom and always remember that she loves you and appreciates you. The love she has for you will never be taken away with dementia. That’s locked in forever.

Hang in there and be strong!! ❤

You’re doing a wonderful job with your mom and always remember that she loves you and appreciates you. The love she has for you will never be taken away with dementia. That’s locked in forever. 

Hang in there and be strong!! ❤
